In practice, targets only receive conversation history or state. They do not get caller identity or caller type.

### Frameworks and protocols

- **OpenAI Agents**: The target receives conversation history (`messages` / `items`), including the assistant turn calling the handoff tool and the tool response. No `caller_agent` or `caller_type` exists on the context.
  - [OpenAI Agents handoffs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/handoffs/)
  - [items.py (`HandoffCallItem`)](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/items.py)
  - [handoffs.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/handoffs.py)

- **LangGraph**: The target node receives graph state via `target_node(state)`. Unless user code explicitly sets a caller field in state, the framework passes no caller metadata.
  - [LangGraph multi-agent handoffs](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/agent-handoffs/)
  - [LangGraph Command API](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#command)

- **A2A protocol**: The server receives `SendMessageRequest` with `MessageSendParams` (`message`, `context_id`, `task_id`). The protocol defines no fields for caller identity or caller type.
  - [A2A types.py (`SendMessageRequest`)](https://github.com/google/a2a-python/blob/main/src/a2a/types.py)

### Why the ADK scenario does not demonstrate caller attributes

The `google-adk` scenario in this PR does not show that generic instrumentation can capture `caller.*`:

1. **Test closure leak**: The scenario patches `adk_a2a_compat.send_message(client, *, request, request_metadata=None, context=None)`. That function does not receive `remote_agent` or `parent_agent`. The scenario only gets `caller` by reading `remote_agent` from the outer test function closure. Real instrumentation wrapping `send_message` cannot access it.
2. **Caller instance is not reliably available**: In ADK, `parent_agent` is only set when an agent is statically declared in another agent's `sub_agents` list. It is `None` for root or standalone agents. On peer-to-peer transfers (`transfer_to_agent`), `target.parent_agent` points to the root coordinator rather than the caller agent that initiated the transfer. It is also not used in ADK's newer `Workflow` engine.
3. **No runtime API**: Neither ADK nor `a2a.client` exposes a caller type property.


-----

I propose to remove these two attributes and remove this refinement since in practice it's not going to be reported. we can always add it later

- **OpenAI Agents**: Captures `agent`. `handoff(agent: Agent)` requires an `Agent` instance (`handoff_obj._agent_ref`), and `Agent.as_tool()` sets `tool._is_agent_tool = True` with `tool_origin.type = AGENT_AS_TOOL`.
  - [handoffs.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/handoffs.py)
  - [agent.py (`as_tool`)](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/agent.py)
- **Google ADK**: Captures `agent` on `AgentTool(agent=...)`, which wraps a `BaseAgent` instance.
  - [agent_tool.py](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/src/google/adk/tools/agent_tool.py)
- **LangGraph**: Cannot capture target type. Transfers return `Command(goto="target_name")`, which is just a node name string in the graph. The tool does not know whether the target node is an agent, workflow, or function.
  - [LangGraph Command API](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#command)

Reference scenarios use `agent` everywhere. Neither `workflow` nor `human` is emitted anywhere in the reference suite, and LangGraph omits the attribute entirely.

----

Proposal: let's remove it until it's necessary  (maybe for some other types of transfers,  human approvals, etc)

This would work in the short term if we wanted to describe only transfers that happen as tools and to agents.

It's not always the case - there are other types of transfers:

- **LangGraph [`Command`](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/graph-api#command) returned from a node**: a router or agent node returns `Command(goto=...)` directly, without a tool. Control moves to one or more nodes. 
- **Microsoft Agent Framework [group chat](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/orchestrations/group-chat) and [Magentic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/orchestrations/magentic)**: an orchestrator (round-robin, prompt-based, or a planning manager LLM) picks the next agent, without a tool.

We might also want to use `gen_ai.transfer.*` for other cases, such as human in the loop (transfer to a human), for example LangGraph [`interrupt()`](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/interrupts) and ADK [tool confirmation](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/tools/confirmation/) that is a tool, but target is not an agent. 

So the current proposal is a subset of a bigger problem space. I don't know how well these attributes play out in human-in-the-loop or non-tool transfers, but I think `gen_ai.tool.call.agent.*` would be too narrow and we'd eventually need to replace it.
I had the attribute name narrower resembling tool.call.agent but based on the above reasoning I switched it to the transfer semantics

Keeping `gen_ai.transfer.*` for the control-flow distinction discussed above. This PR remains limited to tool-mediated transfers, now demonstrated by native ADK and OpenAI handoffs as well as agent-as-tool calls. I have not renamed these to `gen_ai.tool.call.agent.*`, since that would bake the current tool-only scope into names we may want to reuse for non-tool transfers. Leaving this thread open for agreement on naming.
